questions.question: What does a food chain show, and what do the arrows mean? Use an example.
questions.expected_answer: A food chain shows feeding relationships, or what eats what. The arrows mean is eaten by, or gives energy to, and point from the food to the eater. For example: grass, arrow, grasshopper, arrow, frog, arrow, snake.

questions.question: Why does every food chain start with a green plant, and where does the energy come from?
questions.expected_answer: Only green plants can make their own food, so they are the producers. They capture energy from the Sun and store it in their food. The energy for the whole chain first comes from the Sun.

questions.question: Explain how energy is transferred along a food chain and why food chains are short.
questions.expected_answer: When an animal eats a plant or another animal, energy passes to it. But each living thing uses most of the energy to stay alive or loses it as heat, so only a small part is passed on. Less energy is left at each step, so chains are short and there are few top consumers.
